marble.name: Line plots with fractions
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8); use operations on fractions to solve problems involving data in line plots (e.g. redistribute total equally)
marble.prompt: If you measured the lengths of several objects to the nearest quarter or eighth of an inch and plotted them on a number line, could they use those measurements to work out totals or share amounts equally?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning to organise and count information by sorting objects into groups and comparing which groups have more or fewer items.

misconceptions: Treating a line plot like a bar graph — showing only the values that occur, side by side as categories, with no continuous scale and no gaps for unobserved values
Adding the measurement fractions by combining numerators and denominators instead of finding a common denominator
Not seeing 'redistribute equally' as total ÷ count (the fair share / mean) — giving a middle value or leaving the data unchanged
Placing marks imprecisely on the scale, or mis-reading the fractional interval (e.g. an eighth for a quarter)
representations: A number-line measurement scale marked in eighths, with an X (or dot) stacked above each measured value — the line plot itself
The same measurements re-expressed over a common denominator (eighths) for totalling
A 'pour together then share equally' image for the equal-redistribution (fair-share/mean) task
A ruler marked in halves/quarters/eighths, showing where the scale of the plot comes from
authoredAnswer: A correct performance: for (1) draws a number-line scale marked in eighths and stacks a mark above each measured value, leaving the positions with no data visible as gaps (not a row of bars); for (2) adds the two fractions using a common denominator (e.g. 4⅜ + 4½ = 8⅞ inches); for (3) totals ¾+½+¼+½ = 2 cups and divides by 4 to get ½ cup each (fair share). A genuine measurement scale with gaps shown, like-denominator

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: On task (1) the child draws the observed lengths as separate adjacent bars/columns with no evenly-spaced number-line scale, omitting the empty positions between values
wrongAnswers.fix: Reteach on the line-plot prerequisite: the axis is a measurement scale like a ruler — every eighth-position exists and must be shown, even where no pencil falls, because a measurement value is not a category

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: On task (2) or (3) the child writes something like ½ + ¾ = 2/6 (or 2/4), adding tops and bottoms rather than re-expressing over eighths first
wrongAnswers.fix: Reteach on the unlike-denominators prerequisite: re-label all the measurements in a common unit (eighths) before adding, and check the result against the scale

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: On task (3) the child reports ½ because it is the most common amount, or picks a beaker's value, rather than totalling to 2 cups and dividing by 4
wrongAnswers.fix: Confront by pouring together and sharing out: combine all the liquid (the total), then share it among the four beakers; 'equally' means total ÷ count — the fair share

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: The line plot is structurally correct but a mark sits at ⅜ where the value is ½, or an eighth is read as a quarter
wrongAnswers.fix: Scaffold, do not reteach: have the child re-read the scale mark and count the eighths from a labelled point; the understanding of the plot is intact, only the placement slipped
